overview: Immunocore Holdings (IMCR) is a commercial-stage biotech headquartered in Abingdon, UK, that pioneered ImmTAX — soluble T cell receptor bispecifics that redirect the immune system to target cancer, infectious disease and autoimmune disease. Founded in 1999, it trades on Nasdaq.

Its first product, KIMMTRAK (tebentafusp), is approved for unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma and has shown a doubling of five-year survival. KIMMTRAK generated $115.9M in Q2 2026 net sales (up 18% year over year), bringing Immunocore close to break-even — a rarity among the stocks tracked here.

The pipeline centers on melanoma expansion: TEBE-AM (tebentafusp in previously treated cutaneous melanoma, Phase 3, topline data by end of 2026), PRISM-MEL-301 (brenetafusp + nivolumab in first-line cutaneous melanoma, Phase 3) and ATOM (adjuvant uveal melanoma, Phase 3). Earlier programs target PRAME-positive tumors, HIV, type 1 diabetes and dermatology.

Investor thesis: IMCR offers a de-risked, revenue-generating base with Phase 3 upside. Success in cutaneous melanoma — a much larger market than uveal melanoma — would transform the growth outlook. The main risks are TEBE-AM execution and whether the platform extends beyond melanoma.

risks.title: TEBE-AM Readout
risks.description: A negative result in cutaneous melanoma would cap KIMMTRAK's growth to the small uveal melanoma market.

risks.title: Single-Product Revenue
risks.description: All revenue comes from KIMMTRAK; any pricing or competitive pressure directly affects the business.

risks.title: HLA Restriction
risks.description: ImmTAX drugs require HLA-A*02:01-positive patients, limiting the addressable population to roughly half of patients.

risks.title: Competition in Melanoma
risks.description: Cutaneous melanoma is crowded with checkpoint inhibitors and cell therapies.

risks.title: Platform Breadth
risks.description: Programs outside oncology (HIV, type 1 diabetes, dermatology) remain early-stage and unproven.

interpretation: Immunocore is essentially break-even (Q2 2026 net loss of just $0.8M) with $880M in cash, so its runway is effectively unlimited at current spending. The investment question is growth, not financing.
